title: Modern Web Guidance 1.0 Launches to Guide AI Coding Agents
summary: Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla, and MDN release Modern Web Guidance 1.0, a free skill set helping AI agents write modern web code and avoid legacy
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla, and MDN released Modern Web Guidance 1.0 to embed web platform expertise into AI coding agents.
- The free skill set covers 250 modern web features and 203 real-world use cases, installed via npx modern-web-guidance@latest.
- Google tests show guided agent runs passed 88% of legacy-scan checks versus 56% unguided, pushing agents off outdated JavaScript patterns.


Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN Web Docs officially launched Modern Web Guidance 1.0 on November 10, 2026, a cross-vendor skill set designed to embed modern web platform expertise directly into AI coding agents. The free tooling addresses a persistent problem: AI models trained on vast legacy codebases default to outdated JavaScript patterns when native, high-performance web platform solutions now exist. Installation requires a single command: npx modern-web-guidance@latest install.


## What Modern Web Guidance 1.0 Includes


The skill set spans 250 modern web features and 203 real-world developer use cases. Coverage is weighted toward the stack layers coding agents frequently mishandle: 140 CSS and layout features, 74 JavaScript and APIs features, and 36 HTML and DOM features. According to the project README, the goal is to steer agents away from bloated JavaScript implementations toward native browser capabilities that deliver better performance and smaller bundle sizes.


A legacy-scan subcommand analyzes existing codebases to flag legacy patterns that can be modernized. The tool scans HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and package.json files for outdated constructs and suggests modern equivalents. In internal Google tests, guided agent runs passed 88% of legacy-scan checks, compared to 56% for unguided runs.


## Release Date and Cross-Vendor Governance


Officially launched on November 10, 2026, Modern Web Guidance 1.0 represents a rare cross-vendor collaboration in the web standards ecosystem. The project is stewarded jointly by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the broader web development community. The README does not specify a formal versioning roadmap but indicates ongoing maintenance and feature additions are planned.


## Why AI Agents Need Modern Web Guidance


Large language models are trained on massive code corpora that include decades of legacy web development patterns. When generating code, agents often reach for older techniques like jQuery for DOM manipulation, table-based layouts, or polyfills for features now natively supported across evergreen browsers. The result is codebases that ship unnecessary JavaScript, lag in performance, and complicate maintenance.


Modern Web Guidance injects browser compatibility data and best practices directly into the agent's context, guiding it toward modern equivalents. For example, an agent might learn to use CSS Grid instead of float-based layouts, the Fetch API instead of XMLHttpRequest, or native form validation instead of custom JavaScript validators. The tool aims to reduce the gap between what agents know from training data and what the current web platform supports.


## Installation and Usage


Installation is streamlined for developers already using npm-based workflows. Run npx modern-web-guidance@latest install to add the skill set to your project. The tool integrates with popular AI coding agents that support external skill injection, including those built on frameworks like LangChain or Microsoft Semantic Kernel. Once installed, the agent can query the guidance database during code generation, surfacing modern patterns and flagging legacy anti-patterns in real time.


- 250 modern web platform features documented with usage examples
- 203 real-world developer use cases mapped to modern APIs
- Legacy-scan command for auditing existing codebases
- Cross-browser compatibility data from MDN and Chrome Platform Status
- Free and open for all developers and coding agent platforms


## What This Means


Modern Web Guidance 1.0 signals a shift in how browser vendors are responding to the rise of AI coding agents. Rather than waiting for model training to catch up with the evolving web platform, Google, Microsoft, and Mozilla are building tools that inject current best practices directly into agent workflows. The 88% pass rate in guided runs versus 56% unguided suggests the approach works, at least for the legacy patterns Google tested. For teams deploying coding agents in production, the tool offers a low-friction way to nudge generated code toward maintainable, performant patterns without manual intervention.
